record.question: Read the passage about journey and solitude by William Hazlitt, and answer the following questions: (a) What did the writer mean by saying 'I am then never less alone than when alone.' (b) Explain what the writer means by saying 'Contemplation' in your own words. (c) What made the writer say he is himself again (be myself again)? (d) Why did the writer prefer being alone? (e) The writer says: 'For once, I like to have it all my own way' explain his reason. (f) What actions produce ill-humour to the writer? (g) Explain in your own words the meaning of: (i) watering-places (ii) elbow-room (h) Give a title to the passage.
